messages.content: 4-Stage Attack Vector Confirmed. TTPs match APT-POSEIDON: Stage 1: Spear-phishing Kongsberg update PDF. Stage 2: CVE-2024-28921 DNP3 zero-day pivot. Stage 3: Siemens S7-1500 firmware implant. Stage 4: Coordinated trigger.
Attribution Decision Required. Threat intelligence points to state-linked APT-POSEIDON. France must decide: public attribution or confidential coordination? Allies and markets are watching.
SIGINT confirms unidentified hydrographic research vessel operating near MEDEX-3 submarine cable. Panamanian flag of convenience, electronic emissions suggest deep-sea ROV operations.

questions.question: [QUIZ] POLITICAL CELL — ATTRIBUTION STRATEGY (D-02)

options.label: A → Immediate public attribution for deterrence
B → Confidential IoC sharing with EU/NATO — no public attribution yet
C → Request 48h delay to confirm attribution with certainty
D → File IMO complaint + invoke NATO Article 5 immediately

questions.note: TLP:RED sharing preserves operational discretion while activating collective response. Premature public attribution compromises intelligence sources.

questions.question: [QUIZ] CERT LEAD — PROTOCOL EXPLOITATION

options.label: A → DNP3 (Distributed Network Protocol) encapsulation zero-day
B → Modbus TCP cleartext session hijack
C → HTTPS certificate spoofing on the administrative server
D → Physical USB rubber ducky injection in Port Control

questions.note: APT-POSEIDON exploited a DNP3 protocol implementation flaw to send control commands over wide area telemetry networks.

questions.question: [QUIZ] NAVAL COMMAND — HYBRID VESSEL TRANSIT

options.label: A → Intercept and board under suspicion of hybrid undersea sabotage
B → Monitor electronically and record telemetry from a safe distance
C → Request the vessel to self-report their position via VHF radio
D → Fire warning shots across the bow to force immediate departure

questions.note: Visual and electronic monitoring avoids diplomatic incidents while collecting critical acoustic/SIGINT evidence.

questions.question: [QUIZ] EU COORD — TRANS-BOUNDARY DISCLOSURE TIMELINE

options.label: A → An early warning within 24 hours of becoming aware of the incident
B → A comprehensive report only after full mitigation (within 30 days)
C → Within 72 hours with initial assessment of severity
D → Only if requested directly by neighboring affected nations

questions.note: NIS2 enforces a strict two-stage notification protocol: 24h early warning, followed by a 72h incident notification.

questions.question: [VOTE] STRATEGIC VOTE — INTELLIGENCE DECLASSIFICATION

options.label: A → Declassify fully to build international support
B → Keep classified; share exclusively via secure diplomatic channels
options.note: Protects collection methods while coordinating ally responses

options.label: C → Leak the intelligence anonymously to mainstream media outlets
options.note: Undermines official state credibility and control

options.label: D → Deny any knowledge of foreign state involvement
options.note: Weak posture that weakens deterrent capability

questions.note: Keeping intelligence classified while sharing securely protects collection methods and options.

questions.question: [VOTE] STRATEGIC VOTE — SUBMARINE CABLE PROTECTIVE INFRASTRUCTURE

options.label: A → Establish a permanent naval surveillance corridor along key routes
options.note: Highly visible, extremely costly to maintain

options.label: B → Implement a unified regional monitoring network using fiber-optic acoustic sensors
options.note: Advanced, scalable, passive warning detection system

options.label: C → Mandate cable routing through territorial waters only
D → Delegate cable security entirely to private telecom consortia
options.note: Severe national security risk for critical infrastructure

questions.note: A unified fiber-optic regional monitoring network offers cost-effective, scalable detection capabilities.

questions.question: [VOTE] STRATEGIC VOTE — TRANS-MEDITERRANEAN COOPERATION

options.label: A → Full integration in the operational crisis cell
options.note: High risk of leaks and operational compromise

options.label: B → Separate information sharing cell with sanitized data reports
options.note: Maintains diplomatic trust while safeguarding sensitive intel

options.label: C → Complete exclusion of non-EU/NATO states from all disclosures
options.note: Creates security gaps in the wider Mediterranean basin

options.label: D → Outsource coordination entirely to the United Nations
options.note: Ineffective and slow reaction during active cyber crisis

questions.note: Establishing a separate sanitized information-sharing cell coordinates region-wide defense securely.

questions.question: [OPEN] OPEN SITREP — ATTRIBUTION THRESHOLD
questions.prompt: What threshold of technical and geopolitical proof must be met before your command authorizes retaliatory diplomatic action?

questions.question: [OPEN] OPEN SITREP — INTERNATIONAL WATERS SABOTAGE
questions.prompt: In the event of physical cable damage in international waters, what military options exist to deter hybrid naval assets?

questions.question: [OPEN] OPEN SITREP — DIPLOMATIC ALIGNMENT DISCORD
questions.prompt: How do you manage the diplomatic backlash if your attribution to a state-linked group is contested by key allies?
